flashcards.q: Why does a multi-stage build reduce final image size?
flashcards.a: Only the final FROM stage's layers ship. Earlier stages (builder, test) with compilers/dev headers exist only during the build and are discarded except for whatever is explicitly COPY --from=<stage> forwarded.

flashcards.q: Does a later RUN rm remove a secret set via ARG/ENV in an earlier layer?
flashcards.a: No. Layers are immutable and additive; the earlier layer containing the secret still exists in the image's layer history and is recoverable via docker history --no-trunc or the raw image tarball.

flashcards.q: Give real before/after image sizes for a Python service going single-stage python:3.12 to distroless multi-stage.
flashcards.a: ~900MB-1.2GB (single-stage w/ toolchain) -> ~150-250MB (python:3.12-slim) -> further -100 to -300MB from multi-stage removing the toolchain -> ~60-150MB on gcr.io/distroless/python3.

flashcards.q: Why do RUN --mount=type=cache package manager caches matter even with correct layer ordering?
flashcards.a: Layer caching only skips a layer that's fully unchanged; the moment the layer must rebuild (e.g. manifest changed), a plain pip/npm install re-downloads everything since its own download cache lived inside the now-invalidated layer. A cache mount persists that download cache across builds independent of layer hits/misses.

flashcards.q: Why doesn't docker exec -it container sh work on a distroless image, and how do you debug one?
flashcards.a: Distroless ships no shell/package manager/coreutils by design. Debug via an ephemeral sidecar sharing the target's namespaces: docker run --pid=container:X --network=container:X busybox sh, or kubectl debug --target for Kubernetes.

flashcards.q: Why do some teams standardize on Debian-slim over Alpine despite Alpine being smaller?
flashcards.a: Alpine uses musl libc instead of glibc; compiled native extensions and DNS resolution (getaddrinfo semantics) have shown real, hard-to-diagnose behavioral differences under musl, so switching purely for size carries unverified risk.

flashcards.q: Why order COPY requirements.txt + RUN pip install before COPY . . instead of copying everything at once?
flashcards.a: COPY layers cache-key on the content of exactly the files copied. Copying the manifest first means that layer (and the install layer after it) stays cached when only application source changes; copying everything at once invalidates the install layer on any file change.

flashcards.q: What's the concrete security benefit of a non-root USER plus dropped capabilities, beyond 'best practice'?
flashcards.a: An RCE via a dependency or app bug runs with the assigned UID. Root with default capabilities and a writable filesystem is one container-escape away from host root; non-root + --cap-drop=ALL + read-only root fs means the same RCE lands unprivileged, unable to write or use dangerous capabilities like CAP_SYS_ADMIN.

flashcards.q: How do you bind to port 80 without running the container as root?
flashcards.a: --cap-add=NET_BIND_SERVICE combined with --cap-drop=ALL and a non-root USER, or simpler: bind to a high port (8080) inside the container and map it to 80 at the host/load-balancer level.

flashcards.q: How do you pass a credential into a docker build without it landing in layer history?
flashcards.a: BuildKit --mount=type=secret,id=X mounted only into the specific RUN step that needs it, invoked via docker build --secret id=X,src=file. Never use --build-arg or ENV for secrets -- both get baked into layer history permanently.
